message.content:
This is a finger-jointed, edge-glued rubberwood board. Rubberwood is a tropical wood, but heading 4407 covers wood sawn or chipped lengthwise, and finger-jointed or edge-glued boards are treated as wood continuously shaped only if they are shaped along edges (heading 4409). Here the edges and ends are straight-cut, so the board is not continuously shaped. That points to heading 4407, with the finger-jointing and edge-gluing within its scope. Heading 4421 or 4418 does not fit because the board is not dedicated to a particular use.

Within 4407, rubberwood is not listed among the named tropical woods in subheading 4407.2x, which covers mahogany, virola, and similar species. It therefore falls under "other tropical wood", which is 4407.29. For 4407.29, the statistical suffixes include 4407.29.0125 for "Jelutong", "Kapur", "Kempas", "Keruing", "Ramin" and similar, and 4407.29.90 for other. Rubberwood is not a named species there, so it goes under "Other," which is 4407.29.90.

Since 2022, 4407.29 has been split into "Other: Planed; sanded; or end-jointed", and I believe rubberwood sanded would fall in 4407.29.80 "Sanded". The 2022 structure under 4407.29 is: 4407.29.01 (Planed), 4407.29.02 (Sanded), and so on. I can't confirm the exact suffix from memory, but my best answer is 4407.29.0190 for other sanded wood, and I'll go with that.

I recall CBP rulings on rubberwood butcher block classifying it in 4407.29.0190 for "Other: Other: Sanded: Other: Other", and I'm going with that.

{"hts_code": "4407.29.0190", "reason": "Straight-cut, edge-glued and finger-jointed sanded rubberwood board not dedicated to a specific use is lumber of other tropical wood, sawn lengthwise, of heading 4407."}
